# A merge stops before the commit so the result can be reviewed. During that
# review the plaintext of a secret only THEY changed is still ours - the finalize
# refreshes it. If the user edits that file in the meantime, two versions exist
# and neither can be picked for them: the finalize refuses and names both ways out.

sesam-repo admin base.txt theirs.txt edited.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# THEIRS changes the secret; OURS only touches the audit log.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add bob'

! exec git merge topic
stderr 'merge changed the vault - run `git commit` to finalize'

# The object is theirs, the plaintext still ours: stale, and status says what
# the finalize will do about it.
exec cat s
stdout 'BASE'
exec sesam status
stdout 'S s'
stdout 'take the incoming version when you finish'

# The user edits it while reviewing.
cp $TMPDIR/edited.txt s
exec sesam status
stdout '! s'
stdout '1 diverged'
stdout 'sesam reveal --all. takes the incoming version, .sesam seal --all. keeps yours'

! exec git commit -m 'merge topic'
stderr '1 secret changed both here and in this merge'
stderr '  s'
stderr 'sesam reveal --all. takes the incoming version'
stderr 'sesam seal --all. keeps yours'
stderr 'git merge --abort. starts over'

# Nothing was decided for them: the plaintext is untouched, the object theirs.
exec cat s
stdout 'MY-EDIT'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'THEIRS'

# Keeping the edit is one explicit command away.
exec sesam seal --all
exec git commit -m 'merge topic'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'MY-EDIT'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec git status --short
! stdout .

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- theirs.txt --
THEIRS
-- edited.txt --
MY-EDIT
